aneesh/entities/ernesto-laclau.md.title: Ernesto Laclau (1935–2014)

aneesh/entities/erving-goffman.md.summary: Erving Goffman (1922–1982): Canadian-American sociologist whose 'interaction order' and 'dramaturgical' framework — front/back regions, face-work, civil inattention — provides the social-structural complement to Tuan's phenomenological account of spatial behavior.
aneesh/entities/erving-goffman.md.title: Erving Goffman (1922–1982)

aneesh/entities/felix-guattari.md.summary: French psychoanalyst and political philosopher (1930–1992); with Deleuze developed anti-psychiatry, schizoanalysis, and assemblage theory; his ecosophical and media-ecological late work anticipates post-human media theory.
aneesh/entities/felix-guattari.md.title: Félix Guattari

aneesh/entities/fernand-braudel.md.summary: French historian (1902–1985) of the Annales school whose work on long-duration (longue durée) historical temporalities and the coupling of human societies to non-human machines (grain, climate, geography) is a key empirical illustration in Bryant's temporal topology.
aneesh/entities/fernand-braudel.md.title: Fernand Braudel

aneesh/entities/florian-lohse.md.summary: Florian Lohse is a German writer and Contraptions Book Club participant whose Notefields Substack applies Venkatesh Rao's history machine framework to personal encounters with civilizational scale — most notably through the Majapahit empire and the Singapore airport.
aneesh/entities/florian-lohse.md.title: Florian Lohse

aneesh/entities/francis-bacon.md.summary: English philosopher and statesman who proposed a systematic reorganization of all the sciences — an Enlightenment precursor to the universal library aspiration.
aneesh/entities/francis-bacon.md.title: Francis Bacon

aneesh/entities/francisco-varela.md.summary: Chilean biologist, neuroscientist, and philosopher (1946–2001); with Maturana developed autopoiesis; later developed enactivism and neurophenomenology, integrating Husserlian phenomenology with cognitive science.
aneesh/entities/francisco-varela.md.title: Francisco Varela

aneesh/entities/franz-r-kempf.md.summary: Franz R. Kempf is a literary scholar at Bard College whose 2015 essay on Kulturkritik reframes the Rousseau-Schiller-Goethe tradition as a self-reflexive rhetorical mode rather than a simple nature-vs-culture binary.
aneesh/entities/franz-r-kempf.md.title: Franz R. Kempf

aneesh/entities/friedrich-schiller.md.summary: Friedrich Schiller (1759–1805) developed Kulturkritik's aesthetic turn, proposing the play drive (Spieltrieb) and aesthetic education as the cure for modern self-alienation — while his own theory of the sublime reveals that this 'cure' generates more culture rather than reconciling nature and culture.
aneesh/entities/friedrich-schiller.md.title: Friedrich Schiller (1759–1805)

aneesh/entities/gary-klein.md.summary: Gary Klein — cognitive psychologist, founder of the Naturalistic Decision Making research tradition, principal developer of the Data-Frame Theory of Sensemaking and the Recognition-Primed Decision model.
aneesh/entities/gary-klein.md.title: Gary Klein

aneesh/entities/gaston-bachelard.md.summary: French philosopher of science and poetic imagination (1884–1962), best known for The Poetics of Space — a phenomenological account of intimate domestic space that runs parallel to Tuan's humanistic geography.
aneesh/entities/gaston-bachelard.md.title: Gaston Bachelard (1884–1962)

aneesh/entities/geoffrey-west.md.summary: Theoretical physicist (b. 1940) at the Santa Fe Institute whose scaling laws for biology and cities — Kleiber's law derivation and the urban superlinear/sublinear exponents — supply the amplification mechanism in 'The Lightening of Intent'.
aneesh/entities/geoffrey-west.md.title: Geoffrey West

aneesh/entities/george-molnar.md.summary: Hungarian-Australian philosopher (1934–1999) whose posthumous account of powers and dispositions provides Bryant with the five-feature framework for machine powers in onto-cartography.
aneesh/entities/george-molnar.md.title: George Molnar

aneesh/entities/giambattista-vico.md.summary: Giambattista Vico (1668–1744) was a Neapolitan philosopher who argued that each civilization must be understood from within through imaginative participation — a proto-hermeneutic challenge to Enlightenment universalism.
aneesh/entities/giambattista-vico.md.title: Giambattista Vico

aneesh/entities/gilles-deleuze.md.summary: French philosopher (1925–1995); with Guattari developed assemblage theory, rhizomatics, and an immanent philosophy of difference and becoming that underpins Bryant's onto-cartography.
aneesh/entities/gilles-deleuze.md.title: Gilles Deleuze

aneesh/entities/giordano-bruno.md.summary: Giordano Bruno (1548-1600) is reread by Rao not as an early modern martyr for science, but as a terminal medieval outlier whose fate marks the extinguishing of a freewheeling pre-modern mode, not the birth of a new worldview.
aneesh/entities/giordano-bruno.md.title: Giordano Bruno (1548-1600)

aneesh/entities/giovanni-boccaccio.md.summary: Italian author, poet, and humanist (1313–1375) — author of The Decameron, the foundational hundred-tale frame narrative of plague-era Florence, and a pioneer of vernacular prose who defended secular storytelling as consolation, moral instruction, and a literature worthy of serving the Muses.
aneesh/entities/giovanni-boccaccio.md.title: Giovanni Boccaccio

aneesh/entities/gottfried-wilhelm-leibni.summary: German polymath and philosopher — inventor of calculus, dreamer of a universal formal language, and Rao's exemplar of 'the first great modernist error': resolving ontological dread into optimism rather than accepting it, making him a tragic reactionary genius.
aneesh/entities/gottfried-wilhelm-leibni.title: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz (1646–1716)

aneesh/entities/graham-harman.md.summary: American philosopher, founder of Object-Oriented Philosophy (OOP/OOO); argues that all objects withdraw from relations and can never be fully grasped by one another; close interlocutor of Bryant in Speculative Realism.
aneesh/entities/graham-harman.md.title: Graham Harman

aneesh/entities/hank-green.md.summary: YouTube creator, co-founder of VidCon and Complexly, and science communicator whose thesis — that social media users aren't addicted to content but are starving for information — is the catalyst for Sathe's social internet essay.
aneesh/entities/hank-green.md.title: Hank Green

aneesh/entities/harold-bloom.md.summary: Harold Bloom (1930–2019) — Yale literary critic, champion of the Western Canon, author of The Anxiety of Influence; best understood as a mystical thinker in the Kabbalistic-Romantic tradition rather than a conventional academic critic.
aneesh/entities/harold-bloom.md.title: Harold Bloom

aneesh/entities/henri-bergson.md.summary: French philosopher (1859–1941) whose commitment to temporal duration over static representation made him, for Massey, a structural enemy of space despite his sympathy with her aims on time and becoming.
aneesh/entities/henri-bergson.md.title: Henri Bergson (1859–1941)

aneesh/entities/henri-lefebvre.md.summary: French Marxist philosopher (1901–1991) whose theory of the social production of space — especially the spatial triad and the critique of abstract space — provides the structural framework for understanding modernity's spatial condition.
aneesh/entities/henri-lefebvre.md.title: Henri Lefebvre (1901–1991)

aneesh/entities/humberto-maturana.md.summary: Chilean biologist and cognitive scientist (1928–2021); with Francisco Varela developed autopoiesis theory, the biology of cognition, and structural coupling — foundational for systems theory, embodied cognition, and Bryant's machine ontology.
aneesh/entities/humberto-maturana.md.title: Humberto Maturana

aneesh/entities/ian-bogost.md.summary: American video game theorist, designer, and philosopher; co-developer with Bryant of the extended media concept; his 'alien phenomenology' — how non-human entities observe and interact with the world — is adopted in Bryant's Onto-Cartography Ch. 3.
aneesh/entities/ian-bogost.md.title: Ian Bogost

aneesh/entities/ian-morris.md.summary: British classical historian and archaeologist at Stanford whose Social Development Index provides a quantitative measure of civilizational capability across 15,000 years.
aneesh/entities/ian-morris.md.title: Ian Morris

aneesh/entities/ibn-khaldun.md.summary: Ibn Khaldun (1332-1406) is reread by Rao not as a proto-sociologist ahead of his time but as a depressed Arab Petrarch — a diagnostic chronicler of civilizational exhaustion rather than an inaugurator of a new science.
aneesh/entities/ibn-khaldun.md.title: Ibn Khaldun (1332-1406)

aneesh/entities/ilya-prigogine.md.summary: Belgian-Russian physical chemist (1917–2003); Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1977; developed the theory of dissipative structures and far-from-equilibrium thermodynamics, establishing the physical basis for self-organizing complexity.
aneesh/entities/ilya-prigogine.md.title: Ilya Prigogine

aneesh/entities/isaac-newton.md.summary: English mathematician and physicist; his famous phrase 'standing on the shoulders of giants' is the foil for Sathe's 'dancing on the shoulders of giants' — Newton's humility as baseline now vs. metaphor for acceleration.
aneesh/entities/isaac-newton.md.title: Isaac Newton (1643–1727)

aneesh/entities/isaiah-berlin.md.summary: Sir Isaiah Berlin (1909–1997), British philosopher and intellectual historian, best known for the fox-hedgehog typology and his essays on liberty and the history of ideas.
aneesh/entities/isaiah-berlin.md.title: Isaiah Berlin

aneesh/entities/ivan-illich.md.summary: Austrian-born philosopher, Catholic priest, and social critic (1926-2002) who argued that institutions and technologies cross from liberating to enslaving — the 'two watersheds' thesis.
aneesh/entities/ivan-illich.md.title: Ivan Illich

aneesh/entities/ivo-velitchkov.md.summary: Ivo Velitchkov — systems thinker, author of the Link & Think Substack newsletter, contributor to the World Machines Project through essays on Fugger, Wedgwood, and Voltaire as engineers of modernity.
aneesh/entities/ivo-velitchkov.md.title: Ivo Velitchkov

aneesh/entities/j-b-jackson.md.summary: J. B. Jackson (1909–1996): American landscape writer and critic who founded Landscape magazine (1951) and pioneered the cultural reading of the American vernacular landscape — roads, mobile homes, roadside architecture, suburban form — as expressions of democratic values and temporal experience.
aneesh/entities/j-b-jackson.md.title: J. B. Jackson (1909–1996)

aneesh/entities/jacques-derrida.md.summary: French philosopher (1930–2004), founder of deconstruction. For Massey, the most charitable of the post-structuralist engagements with space — Derrida treats spacing as positive — but his textual imagination still pulls space toward two-dimensional surface.
aneesh/entities/jacques-derrida.md.title: Jacques Derrida (1930–2004)

aneesh/entities/jakob-fugger.md.summary: Jakob Fugger (1459–1525), German banking magnate whose wealth reached ~2% of European GDP, transformed the monarch-oligarch relationship from divine right to creditor-debtor contract, and pioneered financial legibility tools.
aneesh/entities/jakob-fugger.md.title: Jakob Fugger

aneesh/entities/jakob-von-uexkull.md.summary: Estonian-German biologist (1864–1944) who developed the concept of the Umwelt — the subjective perceptual world of any organism — a key precursor to Bryant's alien phenomenology.
aneesh/entities/jakob-von-uexkull.md.title: Jakob von Uexküll

aneesh/entities/james-somers.md.summary: James Somers, programmer and writer whose blog surfaces underappreciated intellectual tools — including the 1913 Webster's dictionary — and exemplifies the small-web ethos of careful, niche long-form writing.
aneesh/entities/james-somers.md.title: James Somers

aneesh/entities/jane-bennett.md.summary: American political theorist and new materialist; author of Vibrant Matter (2010), which argues for the agency and efficacy of non-human things — a fellow traveler Bryant cites approvingly against discursive materialism.
aneesh/entities/jane-bennett.md.title: Jane Bennett

aneesh/entities/jean-jacques-rousseau.md.summary: Jean-Jacques Rousseau (1712–1778) is the originator of modern Kulturkritik, whose rhetoric of nature versus culture — articulated through the figures of the noble savage and the English garden — established the oxymoronic template for critiquing modernity through modernity's own tools.
aneesh/entities/jean-jacques-rousseau.md.title: Jean-Jacques Rousseau (1712–1778)

aneesh/entities/jean-piaget.md.summary: Swiss developmental psychologist whose work on sensorimotor intelligence, object permanence, and the lag between practical competence and conceptual grasp is Tuan's primary empirical authority in Space and Place Ch. 3.
aneesh/entities/jean-piaget.md.title: Jean Piaget (1896–1980)

aneesh/entities/jeremiah-dittmar.md.summary: American economic historian (LSE / American University) whose empirical work on the printing press as an information technology supplies the print-economics figures in 'The Lightening of Intent'.
aneesh/entities/jeremiah-dittmar.md.title: Jeremiah Dittmar

aneesh/entities/johann-georg-hamann.md.summary: Johann Georg Hamann (1730–1788), 'the Magus of the North,' was the founding anti-rationalist of the German counter-Enlightenment, arguing that all truth is particular, language precedes reason, and passion gives life to abstractions that reason kills.
aneesh/entities/johann-georg-hamann.md.title: Johann Georg Hamann (1730–1788)

aneesh/entities/johann-gottfried-herder..summary: Johann Gottfried Herder (1744–1803) was a German philosopher, theologian, and literary critic who argued that each culture embodies a distinct and incommensurable form of human excellence — a foundational claim for both Romanticism and Berlin's value pluralism.
aneesh/entities/johann-gottfried-herder..title: Johann Gottfried Herder

aneesh/entities/johann-wolfgang-von-goet.summary: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (1749–1832) is the most skeptical of the Kulturkritik thinkers, rejecting the English garden as aesthetically dishonest and proposing instead a dynamic of irreducible polar opposites (Steigerung) in which nature and culture never synthesize but perpetually intensify each other.
aneesh/entities/johann-wolfgang-von-goet.title: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (1749–1832)

aneesh/entities/johannes-fabian.md.summary: German-American anthropologist (b. 1937), author of *Time and the Other* (1983). His concept of the 'denial of coevalness' is central to Massey's Part Three argument against the temporal convening of spatial difference.
aneesh/entities/johannes-fabian.md.title: Johannes Fabian (b. 1937)

aneesh/entities/john-mcphee.md.summary: John McPhee (b. 1931), staff writer at The New Yorker and Princeton professor, whose essay Draft No. 4 demonstrates the proper use of the dictionary as a generative writing tool.
aneesh/entities/john-mcphee.md.title: John McPhee

aneesh/entities/joseph-de-maistre.md.summary: Joseph de Maistre (1753–1821) was the darkest voice of the counter-revolutionary counter-Enlightenment, arguing that men are naturally evil and destructive, that authority must be absolute and irrational, and that all social order ultimately rests on the executioner.
aneesh/entities/joseph-de-maistre.md.title: Joseph de Maistre (1753–1821)

aneesh/entities/josiah-wedgwood.md.summary: Josiah Wedgwood (1730–1795), English potter who industrialized ceramics, pioneered modern marketing and branding, advanced industrial legibility, and contributed to both the Modernity Machine and (through the Lunar Society) the Divergence Machine.
aneesh/entities/josiah-wedgwood.md.title: Josiah Wedgwood

aneesh/entities/justus-moser.md.summary: Justus Möser (1720–1794) was the first historical sociologist, arguing that each age, each locality has its own irreducible style (Zeitstil, Volksstil) that must be understood holistically — a conservative pluralism that anticipates both Herder and Burke.
aneesh/entities/justus-moser.md.title: Justus Möser (1720–1794)

aneesh/entities/karl-jaspers.md.summary: German-Swiss philosopher (1883-1969) who coined the 'Axial Age' concept — the thesis that simultaneous, independent breakthroughs in reflexive consciousness occurred across multiple civilizations circa 800-200 BCE.
aneesh/entities/karl-jaspers.md.title: Karl Jaspers

aneesh/entities/karl-weick.md.summary: Karl E. Weick — organizational theorist at the University of Michigan, known for sensemaking theory, loose coupling, and enactment; author of 'What Theory Is Not, Theorizing Is' (1995).
aneesh/entities/karl-weick.md.title: Karl E. Weick

aneesh/entities/kei-kreutler.md.summary: Writer, researcher, and theorist working at the intersection of artificial memory, decentralization, and mythopoetics — Sathe cites her on artificial memory as a 'deliberate break in the surface of infinity' that enables navigation rather than mere storage.
aneesh/entities/kei-kreutler.md.title: Kei Kreutler

aneesh/entities/kevin-lynch.md.summary: Kevin Lynch (1918–1984): American urban planner and theorist whose Image of the City (1960) established the five elements of urban cognitive maps (paths, edges, districts, nodes, landmarks) and introduced the concept of 'imageability' as a design criterion.
aneesh/entities/kevin-lynch.md.title: Kevin Lynch (1918–1984)

aneesh/entities/kierkegaard.md.summary: Søren Kierkegaard (1813–1855), Danish philosopher and proto-existentialist, whose conception of anxiety as the dizziness of freedom is foundational to The Plato Plateau.
aneesh/entities/kierkegaard.md.title: Kierkegaard

aneesh/entities/leo-breiman.md.summary: Statistician and machine learning researcher (1928–2005), creator of the random forest algorithm and author of the influential 'Two Cultures' paper diagnosing a split in statistical practice.
aneesh/entities/leo-breiman.md.title: Leo Breiman

aneesh/entities/levi-bryant.md.summary: Levi R. Bryant is an American philosopher working in Speculative Realism and Object-Oriented Ontology; his 'machine-oriented ontology' argues that all entities — material and immaterial — are machines that operate on inputs and produce outputs, forming ecologies through structural coupling.
aneesh/entities/levi-bryant.md.title: Levi R. Bryant

aneesh/entities/liang-qichao.md.summary: Chinese reformist intellectual who envisioned a modern Chinese state in the late Qing dynasty — the intellectual counterpart to the revolutionary figures Sun Yat-sen and Mao Zedong.
aneesh/entities/liang-qichao.md.title: Liang Qichao

aneesh/entities/louis-althusser.md.summary: French Marxist philosopher (1918–1990). For Massey, his critique of Hegel's 'essential section' opens a useful conceptual move — distinguishing closed totality from genuine temporality — but his own theoretical vocabulary still treats 'space' largely as the term for closure.
aneesh/entities/louis-althusser.md.title: Louis Althusser (1918–1990)

aneesh/entities/lunar-society.md.summary: The Lunar Society of Birmingham (c. 1765–1813) — an informal network of industrialists, scientists, and philosophers who met monthly; cited as an early institution of the Divergence Machine's pluralist, experimental ethos.
aneesh/entities/lunar-society.md.title: Lunar Society of Birmingham

aneesh/entities/mahatma-gandhi.md.summary: Indian independence leader who uniquely embodied both the intellectual and revolutionary roles — the exceptional case in the typology of intellectual-revolutionary dyads.
aneesh/entities/mahatma-gandhi.md.title: Mahatma Gandhi

aneesh/entities/majapahit-empire.md.summary: Majapahit was a Hindu-Buddhist maritime empire centered on Java (13th-15th century) notable for its cosmopolitan culture, advanced naval technology, deliberate erasure by Portuguese colonizers, and rich afterlife as the symbolic foundation of modern Indonesia and Balinese culture.
aneesh/entities/majapahit-empire.md.title: Majapahit Empire

aneesh/entities/marcus-aurelius.md.summary: Roman emperor (121-180 CE) and Stoic philosopher whose *Meditations* — written to himself on campaign during the Marcomannic Wars while the Antonine Plague reached the army and his children died one after another — Sathe uses as the figure of the perma-container in its working form: a man for whom the Stoic logos was not a coping technique but a working description of how the universe was actually arranged.
aneesh/entities/marcus-aurelius.md.title: Marcus Aurelius (121–180 CE)

aneesh/entities/maria-popova.md.summary: Maria Popova is the founder of The Marginalian (formerly Brain Pickings) — a long-form blog synthesizing ideas from literature, science, philosophy, and art, known for deep excavations of forgotten works and an emphasis on how to live.
aneesh/entities/maria-popova.md.title: Maria Popova

aneesh/entities/marshall-mcluhan.md.summary: Canadian media theorist (1911–1980); his 'the medium is the message' — that the material properties of media, not their content, shape social relations — is a foundational source for Bryant's post-human media ecology.
aneesh/entities/marshall-mcluhan.md.title: Marshall McLuhan

aneesh/entities/martin-heidegger.md.summary: German phenomenologist (1889–1976), author of Being and Time; his later work on dwelling, technology, and language is the philosophical source for applying phenomenological concepts to knowledge work and product design.
aneesh/entities/martin-heidegger.md.title: Martin Heidegger

aneesh/entities/mau-piailug.md.summary: Satawalese master navigator (c. 1932–2010). Last practitioner of traditional Polynesian non-instrument long-distance wayfinding at the time the craft was revived. Navigated the 1976 Hōkūleʻa voyage from Hawai'i to Tahiti, reopening a practice that had been lost in native Hawaiian tradition for about six centuries, and trained Nainoa Thompson, who in 1980 became the first native Hawaiian long-distance wayfinder in that span.
aneesh/entities/mau-piailug.md.title: Pius "Mau" Piailug (c. 1932–2010)

aneesh/entities/mayo-clinic.md.summary: A leading US academic medical center cited as a flagship institution treating knowledge graphs as the path forward for clinical AI — representing the vanguard of healthcare's adoption of structured knowledge infrastructure.
aneesh/entities/mayo-clinic.md.title: Mayo Clinic

aneesh/entities/michel-de-certeau.md.summary: French Jesuit historian and social theorist (1925–1986), author of *The Practice of Everyday Life* (1984). For Massey, his strategy/tactic distinction maps space onto power and time onto resistance — a binary that traps both terms and fails to think space as eventful.
aneesh/entities/michel-de-certeau.md.title: Michel de Certeau (1925–1986)

aneesh/entities/michel-de-montaigne.md.summary: Michel de Montaigne (1533–1592), French Renaissance writer who invented the personal essay form and modeled a philosophy of frank self-examination and epistemic humility.
aneesh/entities/michel-de-montaigne.md.title: Michel de Montaigne

aneesh/entities/michel-foucault.md.summary: French philosopher (1926–1984) whose analytics of power/knowledge, genealogy of disciplinary institutions, and concept of biopolitics have been foundational for critical theory; Bryant's gravity framework extends and partially critiques Foucault by adding the non-discursive, material-infrastructural dimension of power.
aneesh/entities/michel-foucault.md.title: Michel Foucault (1926–1984)

aneesh/entities/michel-serres.md.summary: French philosopher of science and communication (1930–2019) whose accounts of vortexes, noise, and topological time — especially the 'crumpled handkerchief' — are central to Bryant's spatial and temporal topology.
aneesh/entities/michel-serres.md.title: Michel Serres

aneesh/entities/ming-dynasty-grand-secre.summary: Officials in the Ming dynasty who officially 'merely recorded imperial decisions' while wielding enormous de facto governing power — a paradigm case of antimemetic bureaucratic authority.
aneesh/entities/ming-dynasty-grand-secre.title: Ming Dynasty Grand Secretaries

aneesh/entities/mircea-eliade.md.summary: Romanian historian of religion whose concept of sacred consecration — the ritual act that incorporates new territory into a divine cosmos, erasing its prior existence — provides the religious-historical dimension of place-making through language and ceremony.
aneesh/entities/mircea-eliade.md.title: Mircea Eliade

aneesh/entities/mughal-administration.md.summary: The administrative apparatus of the Mughal Empire, notable for its matrix reporting structure where provincial officials reported directly to the central government rather than to the provincial governor — a designed mechanism for central control and diffused accountability.
aneesh/entities/mughal-administration.md.title: Mughal Administration

aneesh/entities/niccolo-machiavelli.md.summary: Florentine political thinker (1469–1527); in this wiki he appears primarily not as political theorist but as exemplar of the studiolo practice — nightly ritual of intellectual communion with ancient authors.
aneesh/entities/niccolo-machiavelli.md.title: Niccolò Machiavelli

aneesh/entities/nick-cave.md.summary: Australian musician and writer whose open letter arguing that AI creativity is soulless became an unexpected entry point for Sathe's argument about taste as an irreducibly experience-dependent faculty.
aneesh/entities/nick-cave.md.title: Nick Cave

aneesh/entities/niklas-luhmann.md.summary: German sociologist (1927–1998) whose systems theory treats society as composed solely of communications, autopoietically reproducing itself through recursive operations — a position Bryant's onto-cartography explicitly criticizes for neglecting material mediators.
aneesh/entities/niklas-luhmann.md.title: Niklas Luhmann

aneesh/entities/paul-carter.md.summary: Australian cultural historian whose The Road to Botany Bay (1988) argued that European exploration of Australia was constituted by the act of naming — that place emerged through spatial history, not through material transformation.
aneesh/entities/paul-carter.md.title: Paul Carter

aneesh/entities/paul-feyerabend.md.summary: Austrian philosopher of science known for epistemological anarchism — the claim that no single scientific method is universal and that 'anything goes' in productive inquiry — invoked as the epistemological correlate of dancer-style curiosity.
aneesh/entities/paul-feyerabend.md.title: Paul Feyerabend (1924–1994)

aneesh/entities/paul-ricoeur.md.summary: French hermeneutic philosopher whose account of feeling as 'strange intentionality' — directed outward toward things while also inwardly manifesting — grounds Tuan's understanding of how place-attachment is both about the world and about the self.
aneesh/entities/paul-ricoeur.md.title: Paul Ricoeur (1913–2005)

aneesh/entities/perplexity-ai.md.summary: An AI-powered search and answer engine that attempts to restore citations to LLM-generated responses — cited by Sathe as the most credible attempt to address the citation problem in LLMs, though with skepticism about whether it solves the underlying trust issue.
aneesh/entities/perplexity-ai.md.title: Perplexity AI

aneesh/entities/primekg.md.summary: A multimodal precision medicine knowledge graph that integrates multiple domain-specific KGs to enable cross-domain clinical reasoning — cited as an example of the kind of shared knowledge infrastructure that could accelerate healthcare.
aneesh/entities/primekg.md.title: PrimeKG

aneesh/entities/quentin-meillassoux.md.summary: French philosopher associated with Speculative Realism; author of After Finitude (2008), which introduced the concept of correlationism and argued for the speculative necessity of contingency.
aneesh/entities/quentin-meillassoux.md.title: Quentin Meillassoux

aneesh/entities/rabindranath-tagore.md.summary: Bengali polymath — poet, novelist, educator, composer, and philosopher — who shaped Indian national identity and spirituality as an intellectual rather than a revolutionary organizer.
aneesh/entities/rabindranath-tagore.md.title: Rabindranath Tagore

aneesh/entities/richard-mcelreath.md.summary: Evolutionary anthropologist and statistician at the Max Planck Institute, author of 'Statistical Rethinking' — a Bayesian methods textbook that grounds causal inference in scientific epistemology and argues for honesty about model assumptions.
aneesh/entities/richard-mcelreath.md.title: Richard McElreath

aneesh/entities/richard-stallman.md.summary: Richard Stallman (b. 1953), founder of the Free Software Foundation and GNU Project, whose definition of hacking as 'playfully doing something difficult' anchors the Hack Hacky Hacker typology.
aneesh/entities/richard-stallman.md.title: Richard Stallman

aneesh/entities/robert-peake.md.summary: Robert Peake, contemporary poet and participant in the Summer of Protocols, who applied the infinite game framework to poetry and creative practice.
aneesh/entities/robert-peake.md.title: Robert Peake

aneesh/entities/robert-putnam.md.summary: Robert Putnam (b. 1941) is an American political scientist best known for Bowling Alone (2000), which documented the decline of social capital and civic engagement in America over the second half of the 20th century.
aneesh/entities/robert-putnam.md.title: Robert Putnam

aneesh/entities/ron-wakkary.md.summary: Canadian design researcher (b. 1960s) whose concept of 'more-than-human design' argues that designed things exceed their designers' intentions and must be understood as participants in ongoing relationships rather than completed objects.
aneesh/entities/ron-wakkary.md.title: Ron Wakkary

aneesh/entities/simon-willison.md.summary: British developer and writer; creator of Datasette; prominent practitioner and theorist of ethical link blogging as a form of intellectual curation.
aneesh/entities/simon-willison.md.title: Simon Willison

aneesh/entities/stacy-alaimo.md.summary: American feminist environmental humanities scholar who developed the concept of 'trans-corporeality' — the inseparability of human bodies from their more-than-human material environment — cited by Bryant as a key concept for inter-machine material entanglement.
aneesh/entities/stacy-alaimo.md.title: Stacy Alaimo

aneesh/entities/stephen-fry.md.summary: English actor, writer, and public intellectual; in this corpus, notable as the narrator of Nick Cave's AI letter — and as a figure whose own public skepticism about AI dovetails with Cave's position.
aneesh/entities/stephen-fry.md.title: Stephen Fry

aneesh/entities/susanne-langer.md.summary: American philosopher of mind and symbolism whose account of experience as a construction — not a recording — of reality is the epistemological premise underlying Tuan's experiential perspective.
aneesh/entities/susanne-langer.md.title: Susanne Langer (1895–1985)

aneesh/entities/tarn-adams.md.summary: Creator of Dwarf Fortress — built the game over 20 years while completing a PhD and living on donations, representing an extreme case of sustained individual creative audacity.
aneesh/entities/tarn-adams.md.title: Tarn Adams

aneesh/entities/thomas-nagel.md.summary: Philosopher at NYU, known for 'What Is It Like to Be a Bat?' (1974) — an argument that subjective, first-person experience cannot be captured by objective physical description, used by Sathe as an exemplar of Socratic inquiry on an unsolvable question.
aneesh/entities/thomas-nagel.md.title: Thomas Nagel

aneesh/entities/thomas-paine.md.summary: English-American political pamphleteer whose writing provided key philosophical underpinnings for the American Revolution — exemplifying the intellectual role in the American independence typology.
aneesh/entities/thomas-paine.md.title: Thomas Paine

aneesh/entities/tim-ingold.md.summary: British social anthropologist whose relational vocabulary of correspondence, wayfaring, lines, and the education of attention offers a phenomenological counter-idiom to the World Machines legibility frame.
aneesh/entities/tim-ingold.md.title: Tim Ingold

aneesh/entities/timothy-morton.md.summary: British-American literary theorist and eco-philosopher; originator of 'dark ecology' and the concept of hyperobjects; argues that 'Nature' as a concept must be abandoned for genuinely ecological thought — Bryant engages Morton as a key interlocutor, agreeing on rejecting nature-as-outside while resisting the abandonment of the concept.
aneesh/entities/timothy-morton.md.title: Timothy Morton (b. 1968)

aneesh/entities/ulama.md.summary: Islamic legal and religious scholars who shaped law and public morality across pre-modern Islamic states through interpretive authority — an antimemetic power operating within the bureaucracy rather than above it.
aneesh/entities/ulama.md.title: Ulama

aneesh/entities/umberto-eco.md.summary: Italian semiotician, novelist, and intellectual historian — key figure in the history of language theory and the author of the observation that AI may be a revival of the perfect language dream.
aneesh/entities/umberto-eco.md.title: Umberto Eco

aneesh/entities/vaclav-smil.md.summary: Czech-Canadian environmental scientist (b. 1943) and energy historian whose quantitative accounts of civilisational metabolism — energy, food, materials — are the principal source for the historical energy data in 'The Lightening of Intent'.
aneesh/entities/vaclav-smil.md.title: Vaclav Smil

aneesh/entities/vaughn-tan.md.summary: Vaughn Tan — academic, consultant, and author focused on organizational uncertainty and innovation; creator of the Four Questions of Uncertainty framework used by Commoncog for AI sensemaking.
aneesh/entities/vaughn-tan.md.title: Vaughn Tan

aneesh/entities/venkatesh-rao.md.summary: Venkatesh Rao is the author of the Ribbonfarm and Contraptions newsletters, known for machinic, systems-oriented frameworks applied to history, technology, and culture; key concepts in this wiki include the Divergence Machine, Configurancy, and Liveness.
aneesh/entities/venkatesh-rao.md.title: Venkatesh Rao

aneesh/entities/virginia-tufte.md.summary: Virginia Tufte (1922–2020), linguist and professor, author of Artful Sentences — a 270-page analysis of sentence mechanics placed in the anti-library, awaiting the right reader.
aneesh/entities/virginia-tufte.md.title: Virginia Tufte

aneesh/entities/voltaire.md.summary: Voltaire (1694–1778) — French Enlightenment writer, playwright, and entrepreneur who transformed the intellectual's social role, pioneered celebrity, advanced political and epistemic legibility, and made early contributions to the Divergence Machine through Candide and tolerance campaigns.
aneesh/entities/voltaire.md.title: Voltaire

aneesh/entities/werner-herzog.md.summary: Werner Herzog is a German filmmaker whose philosophical remarks about the jungle — 'the harmony of overwhelming and collective murder' — serve as Rao's touchstone for the authentic relationship between liveness and death that civilization suppresses and New Nature requires.
aneesh/entities/werner-herzog.md.title: Werner Herzog

aneesh/entities/william-baumol.md.summary: William Baumol (1922–2017) was an American economist best known for Baumol's cost disease — the observation that labor-intensive service sectors experience chronic relative price inflation as economy-wide productivity rises.
aneesh/entities/william-baumol.md.title: William Baumol

aneesh/entities/william-zinsser.md.summary: William Zinsser (1922–2015), American writer and writing teacher, author of On Writing Well and Writing to Learn — foundational texts in the series of essays on documentation, dictionaries, and prose craft.
aneesh/entities/william-zinsser.md.title: William Zinsser

aneesh/entities/zach-adams.md.summary: Co-creator of Dwarf Fortress alongside his brother Tarn Adams — handles the business, community, and operational side of Bay 12 Games.
aneesh/entities/zach-adams.md.title: Zach Adams

aneesh/log.md.summary: Append-only chronological record of wiki operations. Each entry starts with ## [YYYY-MM-DD] action | detail for unix-parseable output.
aneesh/log.md.title: Log

aneesh/summaries/a-good-dictionary.md.summary: A practical and philosophical case for richer dictionaries, tracing from Zinsser through McPhee to the superiority of the 1913 Webster's over modern abridged editions.
aneesh/summaries/a-good-dictionary.md.title: A Good Dictionary

aneesh/summaries/ai-explainable-enough.m.summary: Aneesh Sathe argues from product experience that AI must be 'explainable enough' — calibrated to the cognitive level of the domain expert user — rather than fully transparent or fully opaque, yielding an AI-human causal prediction machine.
aneesh/summaries/ai-explainable-enough.m.title: AI: Explainable Enough

aneesh/summaries/baumol-cost-disease-tox.summary: Alex Mayyasi argues that Baumol's cost disease is the underappreciated structural cause of America's rising social isolation — making communal, labor-intensive experiences increasingly expensive while scalable, solitude-inducing products get cheaper.
aneesh/summaries/baumol-cost-disease-tox.term: Why 'Cost Disease' Is the Secret Force Behind America's Toxic Solitude
aneesh/summaries/baumol-cost-disease-tox.title: Why 'Cost Disease' Is the Secret Force Behind America's Toxic Solitude

aneesh/summaries/bayo-akomolafe-the-unti.summary: Bayo Akomolafe's Long Now talk argues that the 'untimely' is not an alternative clock but the excess produced inside time's own disciplinary machinery.
aneesh/summaries/bayo-akomolafe-the-unti.title: Bayo Akomolafe — The Untimely

aneesh/summaries/better-company-than-cae.summary: A personal essay using Montaigne's observation about great men who desire to be known outside their competence as a foil for arguing that curiosity-driven, ego-free learning — 'better company than Caesar' — is the path to genuine happiness.
aneesh/summaries/better-company-than-cae.title: Better Company Than Caesar

aneesh/summaries/beyond-the-dataset.md.summary: Argues that data science must rigorously trace both how data is measured and how comparisons are drawn, or all downstream analysis is untrustworthy.
aneesh/summaries/beyond-the-dataset.md.title: Beyond the Dataset

aneesh/summaries/bldgblog-nakatomi-space.summary: Geoff Manaugh coins 'Nakatomi space' — the hidden near-infinite interior of buildings traversable through non-architectural means — drawing a direct line from Die Hard to the IDF's 2002 'walking through walls' tactic in Nablus as documented by Eyal Weizman.
aneesh/summaries/bldgblog-nakatomi-space.title: Nakatomi Space

aneesh/summaries/books-are-dwellings.md.summary: A short essay arguing that books are categorically different from digital reading — they are 'dwellings' rather than billboard-flashes — and that a book club transforms reading from solitary residence into shared architectural exploration.
aneesh/summaries/books-are-dwellings.md.title: Books Are Dwellings

aneesh/summaries/briefing-xai-human-ai-d.summary: A research briefing on the state of Explainable AI (XAI), identifying a credibility gap between technical faithfulness and human usefulness, the disagreement problem between XAI methods, and the framing of XAI within Responsible AI.
aneesh/summaries/briefing-xai-human-ai-d.term: Briefing: The State of Explainable AI (XAI) and Its Impact on Human-AI Decision-Making
aneesh/summaries/briefing-xai-human-ai-d.title: Briefing: The State of Explainable AI (XAI) and Its Impact on Human-AI Decision-Making

aneesh/summaries/chatbots-bats-broken-or.summary: Argues that LLMs open a new mode of using computers — not just problem-solving but genuine Socratic inquiry — because their conversational, fallible nature enables questioning pre-answered beliefs.
aneesh/summaries/chatbots-bats-broken-or.title: Chatbots, Bats & Broken Oracles

aneesh/summaries/cloister-web-reshaping-.summary: Aneesh Sathe's essay arguing that LLMs create a 'Cloister Web' — a new kind of intellectual-political space that enables bespoke, personalized distribution of ideas, potentially collapsing the historical distinction between intellectual and revolutionary.
aneesh/summaries/cloister-web-reshaping-.term: The Cloister Web: Reshaping the Political Maidan
aneesh/summaries/cloister-web-reshaping-.title: The Cloister Web: Reshaping the Political Maidan

aneesh/summaries/cosmic-evolution-chaiss.summary: Eric Chaisson argues that energy rate density — the rate of free energy flow per unit mass — provides a universal, empirically measurable metric for complexity across all systems, unifying physical, biological, and cultural evolution under a single thermodynamic framework.
aneesh/summaries/cosmic-evolution-chaiss.term: Cosmic Evolution: State of the Science — Eric J. Chaisson (2009)
aneesh/summaries/cosmic-evolution-chaiss.title: Cosmic Evolution: State of the Science — Eric J. Chaisson (2009)

aneesh/summaries/dancing-on-the-shoulder.summary: Sathe argues that combining domain experts, large language models, and knowledge graphs creates a composite material capable of accelerating fields like healthcare that have historically resisted Wright's Law efficiency gains.
aneesh/summaries/dancing-on-the-shoulder.term: Dancing on the Shoulders of Giants
aneesh/summaries/dancing-on-the-shoulder.title: Dancing on the Shoulders of Giants

aneesh/summaries/data-frame-theory-of-se.summary: Klein et al. (2007) present a nine-assertion theory of sensemaking as the reciprocal fitting of data into frames and frames around data, grounded in naturalistic decision-making research across military, medical, and emergency domains.
aneesh/summaries/data-frame-theory-of-se.term: A Data-Frame Theory of Sensemaking — Klein, Phillips, Rall & Peluso (2007)
aneesh/summaries/data-frame-theory-of-se.title: A Data-Frame Theory of Sensemaking — Klein, Phillips, Rall & Peluso (2007)

aneesh/summaries/davis-thats-interesting.summary: Murray S. Davis (1971) argues that great theories succeed not by being true but by being interesting — denying a specific aspect of the audience's taken-for-granted assumptions — and catalogs 12 logical categories of interesting propositions.
aneesh/summaries/davis-thats-interesting.title: That's Interesting! — Murray S. Davis (1971)

aneesh/summaries/divine-documentation.md.summary: Argues that reading documentation is an act of deep empathy — with users, with the past self, and with the future — and extends this to learning prose writing.
aneesh/summaries/divine-documentation.md.title: Divine Documentation

aneesh/summaries/domain-ontologies-knowl.summary: Aneesh Sathe's argument that domain ontologies are not merely useful but essential scaffolding for knowledge graph construction, with applications across biomedical, cultural, and AI domains.
aneesh/summaries/domain-ontologies-knowl.term: Domain Ontologies: Indispensable for Knowledge Graph Construction
aneesh/summaries/domain-ontologies-knowl.title: Domain Ontologies: Indispensable for Knowledge Graph Construction

aneesh/summaries/dwarf-fortress-emacs-ai.summary: Aneesh Sathe's essay arguing that Dwarf Fortress, Emacs, and AI share a common soul as platforms for generative complexity — systems whose value lies not in their parts but in emergent creative possibility.
aneesh/summaries/dwarf-fortress-emacs-ai.term: Dwarf Fortress, Emacs, & AI: The Allure of Generative Complexity
aneesh/summaries/dwarf-fortress-emacs-ai.title: Dwarf Fortress, Emacs, & AI: The Allure of Generative Complexity

aneesh/summaries/engineering-liveness-ve.summary: Venkatesh Rao uses the 'useless machine' — a device whose sole function is to turn itself off — as a minimal model of liveness, arguing that capture resistance is life's foundational property and that 'New Nature' is a regime of technological ecology as murderously competitive as Darwin's tangled bank.
aneesh/summaries/engineering-liveness-ve.title: Engineering Liveness — Venkatesh Rao (2026)

aneesh/summaries/fhir-knowledge-graphs-h.summary: Sathe argues that standard RAG fails healthcare's complexity and proposes pairing FHIR-structured knowledge graphs with advanced RAG and AI agents to produce explainable, context-aware clinical AI.
aneesh/summaries/fhir-knowledge-graphs-h.term: Reimagining AI in Healthcare: Beyond Basic RAG with FHIR, Knowledge Graphs, and AI Agents
aneesh/summaries/fhir-knowledge-graphs-h.title: Reimagining AI in Healthcare: Beyond Basic RAG with FHIR, Knowledge Graphs, and AI Agents

aneesh/summaries/hack-hacky-hacker.md.summary: Constructs a horseshoe topology across hack/hacky/hacker to argue that the 'hacky' middle position — playful, lateral, fox-like — is the optimal life posture.
aneesh/summaries/hack-hacky-hacker.md.title: Hack, Hacky, Hacker

aneesh/summaries/history-machines-in-the.summary: Florian Lohse uses the Majapahit empire and a Singapore airport layover to illustrate Venkatesh Rao's 'history machine' thesis: modernity emerges not from singularly great men but from distributed components assembling silently across centuries until paradigm shift suddenly arrives.
aneesh/summaries/history-machines-in-the.term: History Machines in the Margins — Florian Lohse (2025)
aneesh/summaries/history-machines-in-the.title: History Machines in the Margins — Florian Lohse (2025)

aneesh/summaries/how-experts-sensemake.m.summary: Cedric Chin's application of Klein et al's Data-Frame Theory to expert sensemaking — argues that expert-novice differences lie not in reasoning strategy but in richer mental models, denser frame repertoires, and faster expectancy violation detection.
aneesh/summaries/how-experts-sensemake.m.title: How Experts Sensemake (Chin, 2026)

aneesh/summaries/how-to-make-sense-of-ai.summary: Cedric Chin's practical sensemaking method for navigating AI uncertainty — filter all AI content except detailed field reports of use, then apply the four questions of uncertainty to evaluate possible outcomes, actions, values, and causal mechanisms.
aneesh/summaries/how-to-make-sense-of-ai.term: How to Make Sense of AI (Chin, 2026)
aneesh/summaries/how-to-make-sense-of-ai.title: How to Make Sense of AI (Chin, 2026)

aneesh/summaries/isaiah-berlin-against-t.summary: Isaiah Berlin's Against the Current collects his essays on counter-Enlightenment thinkers — Vico, Hamann, Herder, Machiavelli, Sorel, Maistre — who challenged the monist rationalist tradition, whose pluralism Berlin finds both intellectually serious and politically urgent.
aneesh/summaries/isaiah-berlin-against-t.term: Isaiah Berlin — Against the Current: Essays in the History of Ideas
aneesh/summaries/isaiah-berlin-against-t.title: Isaiah Berlin — Against the Current: Essays in the History of Ideas

aneesh/summaries/jan-10-2025-ai-agents-m.summary: Two parallel threads: a paper arguing current AI agents are insufficient (proposing 'Sims' as user-representing companions), and a meditation on the Renaissance studiolo as a model for private intellectual space and self-cultivation.
aneesh/summaries/jan-10-2025-ai-agents-m.title: Jan 10, 2025 - AI Agents, Machiavelli's Study

aneesh/summaries/jan-3-2025.md.summary: A link-blog digest covering the aesthetics of maximalist blogging, ethical principles for link posts, AI's failure to democratize knowledge, and the philosophical status of probability.
aneesh/summaries/jan-3-2025.md.title: Jan. 3, 2025

aneesh/summaries/jan-7-2025-building-dwe.summary: An application of Heidegger's 'Building Dwelling Thinking' to product design and data science, arguing that good products free users to dwell — to think and explore — rather than conforming them to a tool's constraints.
aneesh/summaries/jan-7-2025-building-dwe.title: Jan. 7, 2025: Building Dwelling Thinking

aneesh/summaries/klein-data-frame-theory.summary: Klein et al's 2007 academic paper establishing the Data-Frame Theory of Sensemaking — eight functions of sensemaking, the data-frame symbiosis, and the four sensemaking cycles, drawn from naturalistic studies of military and medical experts.
aneesh/summaries/klein-data-frame-theory.term: A Data-Frame Theory of Sensemaking (Klein, Phillips, Rall, Peluso, 2007)
aneesh/summaries/klein-data-frame-theory.title: A Data-Frame Theory of Sensemaking (Klein, Phillips, Rall, Peluso, 2007)

aneesh/summaries/looking-forward-to-mont.summary: A brief personal essay contrasting Montaigne's frank, living prose with Byung-Chul Han's diagnosis of narrative commodification, arguing that personal, meandering writing may be the antidote to storyselling.
aneesh/summaries/looking-forward-to-mont.title: Looking Forward to Montaigne

aneesh/summaries/massey-for-space-part-1.summary: Part One of Massey's For Space (2005) opens the case for a relational, open, and always-in-process conception of space by diagnosing three persistent failures of spatial imagination and offering three propositions as the corrective.
aneesh/summaries/massey-for-space-part-1.term: Massey, *For Space* — Part One: Setting the Scene
aneesh/summaries/massey-for-space-part-1.title: Massey, *For Space* — Part One: Setting the Scene

aneesh/summaries/massey-for-space-part-2.summary: Part Two of Massey's *For Space* (2005): a four-chapter critique of philosophical traditions (Bergson, structuralism, Laclau/de Certeau, deconstruction) that imagine space as the dead, the closed, the merely-representational, and a sketch of her constructive alternative — space as a dynamic simultaneity of multiple ongoing trajectories.
aneesh/summaries/massey-for-space-part-2.term: Massey, *For Space* (2005) — Part Two: Unpromising Associations
aneesh/summaries/massey-for-space-part-2.title: Massey, *For Space* (2005) — Part Two: Unpromising Associations

aneesh/summaries/massey-for-space-part-3.summary: Part Three of Massey's *For Space* (2005): five chapters arguing that modernity and neoliberal globalisation both repress space by converting coexisting spatial difference into a single temporal queue — and that the dominant 'aspatial globalisation' narrative is a political weapon, not a description.
aneesh/summaries/massey-for-space-part-3.term: Massey, *For Space* (2005) — Part Three: Living in Spatial Times?
aneesh/summaries/massey-for-space-part-3.title: Massey, *For Space* (2005) — Part Three: Living in Spatial Times?

aneesh/summaries/massey-for-space-part-4.summary: Part Four of Massey's For Space (2005) — Chapters 11 and 12 — develops her constructive positive theory of space and place: space as a simultaneity of on-going trajectories, and place as an event-like throwntogetherness of those trajectories at a particular conjuncture.
aneesh/summaries/massey-for-space-part-4.title: Massey, *For Space*, Part Four: Reorientations (2005)

aneesh/summaries/massey-for-space-part-5.summary: Part Five of Massey's *For Space* (2005): three chapters arguing that recognising space as a sphere of multiplicity makes politics constitutively spatial — places are events of throwntogetherness, no universal rules of space and place can be derived, and time-spaces are continually made and contested.
aneesh/summaries/massey-for-space-part-5.term: Massey, *For Space* (2005) — Part Five: A Relational Politics of the Spatial
aneesh/summaries/massey-for-space-part-5.title: Massey, *For Space* (2005) — Part Five: A Relational Politics of the Spatial

aneesh/summaries/my-grandfather-had-lore.summary: Aneesh Sathe argues that degrading search quality and hallucinating LLMs may produce a civilizational regression toward lore — informal oral expertise — as the default mode of accessing reliable information.
aneesh/summaries/my-grandfather-had-lore.term: My Grandfather Had Lore, My Father Had Google, I Have ChatGPT, My Son Will Have Lore
aneesh/summaries/my-grandfather-had-lore.title: My Grandfather Had Lore, My Father Had Google, I Have ChatGPT, My Son Will Have Lore

aneesh/summaries/my-road-to-bayesian-sta.summary: Aneesh Sathe recounts his conversion from frequentist to Bayesian statistics, driven by the inadequacy of p-values for small-sample biological experiments and the need for transparency about causal assumptions.
aneesh/summaries/my-road-to-bayesian-sta.title: My Road to Bayesian Stats

aneesh/summaries/noble-savages-and-engli.summary: Franz Kempf's scholarly argument that Kulturkritik is not a simple nature-vs-culture binary but a self-reflexive rhetorical mode that uses antithetical scenarios to 'heal from culture through culture,' tracing this paradox through Rousseau, Schiller, and Goethe via the figure of the garden.
aneesh/summaries/noble-savages-and-engli.term: Noble Savages and English Gardeners: Kulturkritik from Rousseau to Goethe
aneesh/summaries/noble-savages-and-engli.title: Noble Savages and English Gardeners: Kulturkritik from Rousseau to Goethe

aneesh/summaries/not-my-lever.md.summary: Aneesh Sathe's essay 'Not My Lever — The Last Container' (2026), arguing that as metaphysical containers have receded across two millennia, modern individuals face a surface of concern five orders of magnitude wider than the cohort psychology was built for, and that the discipline of refusing most levers — paired with a thicket that gives the kept ones real feedback — is the working mode of the Liveness era.
aneesh/summaries/not-my-lever.md.title: Not My Lever — Summary

aneesh/summaries/on-being-good-vs-knowin.summary: Aneesh Sathe uses Nick Cave's critique of AI creativity to articulate a distinction between AI that knows facts and AI that has taste — and argues that taste, rooted in imperfect experience, cannot be engineered.
aneesh/summaries/on-being-good-vs-knowin.term: On Being Good vs. Knowing Good: Perspectives on AI
aneesh/summaries/on-being-good-vs-knowin.title: On Being Good vs. Knowing Good: Perspectives on AI

aneesh/summaries/on-not-knowing-and-payi.summary: Tim Ingold's 2023 essay argues that wisdom (turning toward an uncertain world and paying attention) is opposed to knowledge (turning away to secure prediction), that uncertainty is the excess that makes possibility real, and that not-knowing is a form of wisdom rather than ignorance.
aneesh/summaries/on-not-knowing-and-payi.term: On Not Knowing and Paying Attention
aneesh/summaries/on-not-knowing-and-payi.title: On Not Knowing and Paying Attention

aneesh/summaries/on-protocols-wagons-and.summary: A personal essay on falling off creative habits, recovering them, and the protocol of continuous self-construction through writing.
aneesh/summaries/on-protocols-wagons-and.term: On Protocols, Wagons, and Associated Acrobatics
aneesh/summaries/on-protocols-wagons-and.title: On Protocols, Wagons, and Associated Acrobatics

aneesh/summaries/onto-cartography-bryant.summary: Bryant's account of machines as operational systems (Ch 2) and the alien phenomenology of non-human structural openness (Ch 3).
aneesh/summaries/onto-cartography-bryant.term: Onto-Cartography Ch 2–3: What Is a Machine? / Alien Phenomenology
aneesh/summaries/onto-cartography-bryant.title: Onto-Cartography Ch 2–3: What Is a Machine? / Alien Phenomenology

aneesh/summaries/onto-cartography-bryant.summary: Bryant's account of machines as assemblages of other machines, the endo/exo-relations distinction, entropy and negentropic operations, and the political stakes of machine maintenance.
aneesh/summaries/onto-cartography-bryant.term: Summary: Bryant, *Onto-Cartography* Ch 4 — Machinic Assemblages and Entropy (pp. 75–108)
aneesh/summaries/onto-cartography-bryant.title: Summary: Bryant, *Onto-Cartography* Ch 4 — Machinic Assemblages and Entropy (pp. 75–108)

aneesh/summaries/onto-cartography-bryant.summary: Bryant's account of worlds as real, plural, flat ecologies of machines — not correlated to any subject — structured internally by varying degrees of machine salience (bright/dim/dark/rogue objects) and partitioned by the material conditions of interaction.
aneesh/summaries/onto-cartography-bryant.term: Summary: Onto-Cartography Ch. 5 — The Structure of Worlds
aneesh/summaries/onto-cartography-bryant.title: Summary: Onto-Cartography Ch. 5 — The Structure of Worlds

aneesh/summaries/onto-cartography-bryant.summary: Bryant's Ch. 6 argues that space and time are not containers but products of machine-relations, replacing Cartesian/Euclidean geometry with topological analysis across spatial fields, temporal rhythms, overdetermination, and the politics of fatigue.
aneesh/summaries/onto-cartography-bryant.term: Summary: Bryant, *Onto-Cartography* Ch. 6 — "Topologies of Space and Time" (pp. 140–183)
aneesh/summaries/onto-cartography-bryant.title: Summary: Bryant, *Onto-Cartography* Ch. 6 — "Topologies of Space and Time" (pp. 140–183)

aneesh/summaries/onto-cartography-bryant.summary: Bryant's theory of gravity as the structural power machines exert over the field of possible action for other machines — covering the six object-types, bright/dim/dark/satellite/rogue/black-hole typology, the political stakes of infrastructural over ideological power, and the framework of subjects, quasi-objects, and events.
aneesh/summaries/onto-cartography-bryant.title: Summary: *Onto-Cartography* Ch. 7 — "Gravity" (Bryant 2014, pp. 184–232)

aneesh/summaries/onto-cartography-bryant.summary: Bryant's concluding chapter deploys geophilosophy's three practical dimensions — cartography, deconstruction, and terraformation — as the emancipatory program for a post-humanist left politics adequate to climate collapse.
aneesh/summaries/onto-cartography-bryant.term: Onto-Cartography Ch 8: Earth, Maps, and Practices — Summary
aneesh/summaries/onto-cartography-bryant.title: Onto-Cartography Ch 8: Earth, Maps, and Practices — Summary

aneesh/summaries/onto-cartography-bryant.summary: Bryant's polemic against discursive materialism and introduction of onto-cartography — the mapping of structural couplings between machines — and post-human media ecology as an ecological framework for understanding how entities shape the field of possibility for one another.
aneesh/summaries/onto-cartography-bryant.title: Onto-Cartography: Introduction & Chapter 1 — Summary

aneesh/summaries/problems-are-places-que.summary: Maps Callard's Socratic distinction between problems and questions onto the spatial framework of places and spaces, arguing that problems are bounded, tractable places while questions are open, exploratory spaces.
aneesh/summaries/problems-are-places-que.term: Problems are Places, Questions are Spaces
aneesh/summaries/problems-are-places-que.title: Problems are Places, Questions are Spaces

aneesh/summaries/revolution-in-time.md.summary: Landes argues that demand for precise time — rooted in Western monasticism — pulled the mechanical clock into existence, and that the clock then shaped modernity; the second half traces seven centuries of industry in which simple, reproducible designs repeatedly beat virtuoso masterpieces, while incumbents, from Geneva to Waltham, failed not by bad luck but by failure of imagination.
aneesh/summaries/revolution-in-time.md.term: Revolution in Time — David S. Landes (1983; 1999)
aneesh/summaries/revolution-in-time.md.title: Revolution in Time — David S. Landes (1983; 1999)

aneesh/summaries/royalty-administration-.summary: Traces how royal administrations across history were deliberately antimemetic — powerful but invisible — so that public anger would always target visible rulers, not the bureaucratic machinery doing the real work.
aneesh/summaries/royalty-administration-.title: Royalty, Administration, and Antimemetics

aneesh/summaries/shitty-castles.md.summary: Florian Lohse's essay arguing that elaborate intellectual and material constructions built by people who know they won't hold — 'shitty castles' — are not necessarily hypocritical but can serve pragmatic functions of power, stability, and temporal bridging.
aneesh/summaries/shitty-castles.md.term: Shitty Castles: On the Art of Digging Fake Moats
aneesh/summaries/shitty-castles.md.title: Shitty Castles: On the Art of Digging Fake Moats

aneesh/summaries/social-internet-lost-an.summary: Diagnoses social media's failure as a mismatch between information hunger (a biological need for orientation) and the noise-maximizing incentives of platform companies, proposing Socratic inquiry as the corrective posture.
aneesh/summaries/social-internet-lost-an.title: Social Internet — Lost and Hungry

aneesh/summaries/the-architecture-of-res.summary: Aneesh Sathe traces three historical moments — Spinoza's Amsterdam, Adonis's Beirut, and 2025's AI-mediated internet — to argue that resistance against the averaging power of dominant systems requires cultivating 'thickets': deliberately opaque, friction-rich habitats that protect divergence.
aneesh/summaries/the-architecture-of-res.title: The Architecture of Resistance

aneesh/summaries/the-arrival-of-composab.summary: A historical survey of how knowledge transmission evolved from oral tradition to digital repositories, arguing that composability — the ability to combine and recombine information into new understanding — has been the throughline of intellectual progress.
aneesh/summaries/the-arrival-of-composab.title: The Arrival of Composable Knowledge

aneesh/summaries/the-best-game-ever-made.summary: A meditation on Dwarf Fortress as an act of creative audacity — a hyper-complex simulation built by two brothers over 20 years without external funding, arguing the game's value lies in its stories rather than any victory condition.
aneesh/summaries/the-best-game-ever-made.title: The Best Game Ever Made

aneesh/summaries/the-best-of-all-possibl.summary: Florian Lohse's essay-as-fable, structured in three scenes, that uses Voltaire's Candide and Panglossian optimism as a lens on techno-optimism, the limits of zoomed-out reasoning, and the alternative of tending a small thicket instead of optimizing for civilizational scale.
aneesh/summaries/the-best-of-all-possibl.term: The Best of All Possible Worlds: On Gambas, Gardening and Panglossian Optimism
aneesh/summaries/the-best-of-all-possibl.title: The Best of All Possible Worlds: On Gambas, Gardening and Panglossian Optimism

aneesh/summaries/the-decameron.md.summary: Giovanni Boccaccio's hundred-tale cycle (c. 1349–1353): seven young women and three young men flee plague-struck Florence in 1348 to a country estate, where over ten days they govern themselves as a rotating monarchy and tell a hundred stories — a frame that stages storytelling as both consolation and world-maintenance, ranges across wit, fortune, desire, trickery, and magnificence, and closes with the deliberate dissolution of the company and Boccaccio's defence of his own book.
aneesh/summaries/the-decameron.md.title: The Decameron

aneesh/summaries/the-divergence-machine..summary: Venkatesh Rao's introductory essay for his 2026 Contraptions Book Club, laying out a grand theory of world machines — the modernity machine now declining and the divergence machine now ascending — and a taxonomy of the intellectual currents inhabiting this transition (late modernity, postmodernity, metamodernity, divergentism).
aneesh/summaries/the-divergence-machine..term: The Divergence Machine: Introducing the 2026 Book Club Theme
aneesh/summaries/the-divergence-machine..title: The Divergence Machine: Introducing the 2026 Book Club Theme

aneesh/summaries/the-end-of-identity-ai-.summary: Aneesh Sathe reads the history of philosophy through Venkatesh Rao's Divergence Machine framework to argue that AI completes the centuries-long peeling back of identity — stripping the last layer of legible selfhood and demanding genuine plasticity rather than mere flexibility.
aneesh/summaries/the-end-of-identity-ai-.term: The End of Identity: AI, Plasticity, and the Divergence Machine
aneesh/summaries/the-end-of-identity-ai-.title: The End of Identity: AI, Plasticity, and the Divergence Machine

aneesh/summaries/the-influence-of-anxiet.summary: A personal-critical essay on Harold Bloom's Anxiety of Influence — argues that Bloom is fundamentally a mystical thinker, that his theory of poetic influence-as-agon is both necessary and paralyzing, and that the only way out of the anxiety is through it, not around it.
aneesh/summaries/the-influence-of-anxiet.title: The Influence of Anxiety (The Point, ~2022–2024)

aneesh/summaries/the-lightening-of-inten.summary: Aneesh Sathe's essay 'The Lightening of Intent' (2026), a Contraptions Book Club piece arguing that the cost of putting an idea into the world has fallen ~5 orders of magnitude across 25 centuries while the energy rate density of the underlying system has risen monotonically — and that the next bottleneck after atoms and ideas is intent itself, contingent on whether the fossil-to-solar energy transition holds.
aneesh/summaries/the-lightening-of-inten.title: The Lightening of Intent — Summary

aneesh/summaries/the-mind-as-semi-solid-.summary: Turns the space-and-place lens inward: the mind is an imperfect, self-conjured place whose navigational landmarks are semi-solid smoke — a feature enabled by normative self-blindness that makes Socratic inquiry both necessary and initially threatening.
aneesh/summaries/the-mind-as-semi-solid-.title: The Mind as Semi-Solid Smoke

aneesh/summaries/the-plato-plateau.md.summary: Argues that people select philosophical frameworks matching their current degree of identity disruption, using Kierkegaard's anxiety as the generative motor.
aneesh/summaries/the-plato-plateau.md.title: The Plato Plateau

aneesh/summaries/the-shelter-as-epistemi.summary: Aneesh Sathe argues that 'home' — whether literal shelter, a published paper, or a foundational thesis — is not a retreat from the unknown but an active epistemic engine that converts abstract space into navigable place.
aneesh/summaries/the-shelter-as-epistemi.title: The Shelter as Epistemic Engine

aneesh/summaries/the-small-god-of-the-in.summary: A mythopoeic essay personifying RSS as a minor deity of the open web — patient, orderly, and slowly marginalized by platform capitalism — and an argument for its revival as the proper technology of reading.
aneesh/summaries/the-small-god-of-the-in.term: The Small God of the Internet
aneesh/summaries/the-small-god-of-the-in.title: The Small God of the Internet

aneesh/summaries/the-tortured-artist-is-.summary: Argues that the 'tortured artist' archetype — solitary, suffering, perfecting — is an artifact of print culture that LLMs and collaborative creative forms are rendering obsolete; what replaces it is courage, commitment, and collaborative risk-taking.
aneesh/summaries/the-tortured-artist-is-.term: The Tortured Artist Is So Yesterday
aneesh/summaries/the-tortured-artist-is-.title: The Tortured Artist Is So Yesterday

aneesh/summaries/the-viscous-frontier.md.summary: Aneesh Sathe's essay 'The Viscous Frontier: How to Move When the Machine Stops Pulling' (2026), a companion piece to Rao's Divergence Machine series. Uses Purcell's 1977 scallop theorem as the physical model for why cultural motion in the Divergence Machine is viscous, why dissipative structures like the attention economy produce no net displacement, and why the architectural requirement to leave an artifact is the cultural equivalent of the flagellum.
aneesh/summaries/the-viscous-frontier.md.title: The Viscous Frontier — Summary

aneesh/summaries/the-world-machines-proj.summary: Venkatesh Rao's announcement of the World Machines Project — a collaborative nonfiction extended universe built around the World Machines framework, growing out of the Contraptions Book Club.
aneesh/summaries/the-world-machines-proj.title: The World Machines Project

aneesh/summaries/thinking-with-places.md.summary: Argues that thinking is fundamentally place-making — the act of interrupting undifferentiated possibility-space with knowledge-anchored landmarks — and that Socratic dialogue is cartography applied to belief.
aneesh/summaries/thinking-with-places.md.title: Thinking with Places

aneesh/summaries/three-engineers-of-mode.summary: Ivo Velitchkov profiles Jakob Fugger, Josiah Wedgwood, and Voltaire as engineers of the Modernity Machine, arguing each transformed class relations and advanced legibility — while Wedgwood and Voltaire also made early commits to the Divergence Machine.
aneesh/summaries/three-engineers-of-mode.title: Three Engineers of Modernity

aneesh/summaries/tuan-1991-language-and-.summary: Tuan argues that language — speech, naming, narrative — is constitutive of place-making, not merely descriptive: without words, places cannot fully come into being or persist in human consciousness.
aneesh/summaries/tuan-1991-language-and-.term: Tuan (1991): Language and the Making of Place: A Narrative-Descriptive Approach
aneesh/summaries/tuan-1991-language-and-.title: Tuan (1991): Language and the Making of Place: A Narrative-Descriptive Approach

aneesh/summaries/tuan-2002-space-and-pla.summary: Primary-text summary of Tuan's Space and Place Chapters 1–3: the experiential approach, modes of sensory knowing, and the developmental psychology of space and place in the child.
aneesh/summaries/tuan-2002-space-and-pla.term: Tuan, *Space and Place: The Perspective of Experience* — Chapters 1–3
aneesh/summaries/tuan-2002-space-and-pla.title: Tuan, *Space and Place: The Perspective of Experience* — Chapters 1–3

aneesh/summaries/tuan-2002-space-and-pla.summary: Primary-text summary of Tuan's Space and Place Chapters 10–12: intimate place, attachment to homeland, and the mechanisms by which places acquire public visibility.
aneesh/summaries/tuan-2002-space-and-pla.term: Tuan, *Space and Place: The Perspective of Experience* — Chapters 10–12
aneesh/summaries/tuan-2002-space-and-pla.title: Tuan, *Space and Place: The Perspective of Experience* — Chapters 10–12

aneesh/summaries/tuan-2002-space-and-pla.summary: Tuan's final two chapters argue that place and time mutually constitute each other — place is the pause in movement, and temporal depth is what elevates a locale into a place — then the epilogue reflects on what the experiential method achieves and what it cannot reach.
aneesh/summaries/tuan-2002-space-and-pla.term: Tuan, *Space and Place* — Ch 13 (Time and Place) & Ch 14 (Epilogue)
aneesh/summaries/tuan-2002-space-and-pla.title: Tuan, *Space and Place* — Ch 13 (Time and Place) & Ch 14 (Epilogue)

aneesh/summaries/tuan-2002-space-and-pla.summary: Summary of Chapters 4–6 of Yi-Fu Tuan's Space and Place (1977/2002): the body as origin of spatial values, spaciousness and crowding as social rather than geometric phenomena, and the spectrum from spatial ability to cognitive map-making.
aneesh/summaries/tuan-2002-space-and-pla.title: Tuan — *Space and Place*, Chapters 4–6 (1977/2002)

aneesh/summaries/tuan-2002-space-and-pla.summary: Primary-text summary of Tuan's Space and Place Chapters 7–9: mythical space as cosmological matrix, architecture as crystallized awareness, and time as the animating dimension of experiential place.
aneesh/summaries/tuan-2002-space-and-pla.term: Tuan, *Space and Place: The Perspective of Experience* — Chapters 7–9
aneesh/summaries/tuan-2002-space-and-pla.title: Tuan, *Space and Place: The Perspective of Experience* — Chapters 7–9

aneesh/summaries/universal-library-river.summary: Aneesh Sathe's essay tracing the myth of the universal library from Alexandria through LLMs, arguing that noise in information systems is generative rather than purely destructive.
aneesh/summaries/universal-library-river.term: The Universal Library in the River of Noise
aneesh/summaries/universal-library-river.title: The Universal Library in the River of Noise

aneesh/summaries/usc-ai-homogenization-c.summary: USC researchers argue that widespread LLM use is homogenizing human cognition — standardizing language, reasoning styles, and perspectives — and that this reduction in cognitive diversity threatens collective intelligence and adaptive capacity.
aneesh/summaries/usc-ai-homogenization-c.term: AI May Be Making Us Think and Write More Alike
aneesh/summaries/usc-ai-homogenization-c.title: AI May Be Making Us Think and Write More Alike

aneesh/summaries/venkatesh-rao-the-diver.summary: Rao introduces the 'Argument of Progress' as the Divergence Machine's alternative to Fiat Progress narratives, using Spinoza vs. Leibniz and Hume vs. Smith to trace how Progress became a non-stationary, pluralist, reality-driven argument.
aneesh/summaries/venkatesh-rao-the-diver.term: The Divergence Machine II: Progress as a Non-Stationary Argument (Rao, Feb 2026)
aneesh/summaries/venkatesh-rao-the-diver.title: The Divergence Machine II: Progress as a Non-Stationary Argument (Rao, Feb 2026)

aneesh/summaries/venkatesh-rao-the-moder.summary: A mid-year book club update in which Rao refines his world-machine periodization thesis, using global parallel examples (Battle of Talikota, Indian Reformation movements) to illustrate horizontal history in action.
aneesh/summaries/venkatesh-rao-the-moder.title: The Modernity Machine II (Rao, Jun 2025)

aneesh/summaries/venkatesh-rao-the-moder.summary: The concluding installment of Rao's trilogy on the Modernity Machine, arguing it optimized for legibility rather than truth or freedom, and that its own success made internal repair impossible, necessitating the Divergence Machine.
aneesh/summaries/venkatesh-rao-the-moder.term: The Modernity Machine III: Completion, Saturation, and Phase Transition (Rao, Dec 2025)
aneesh/summaries/venkatesh-rao-the-moder.title: The Modernity Machine III: Completion, Saturation, and Phase Transition (Rao, Dec 2025)

aneesh/summaries/venkatesh-rao-the-moder.summary: Rao argues that modernity began not in the 16th century but in the 13th, framing it as a global civilizational machine assembled across six shifting class relationships between 1200 and 1600.
aneesh/summaries/venkatesh-rao-the-moder.title: The Modernity Machine (Rao, Jan 2025)

aneesh/summaries/voltaire-the-entreprene.summary: Ivo Velitchkov recounts how Voltaire at 76 founded a successful international watchmaking enterprise at Ferney, arguing he belongs alongside Fugger and Wedgwood as a pre-industrial entrepreneur and engineer of modernity.
aneesh/summaries/voltaire-the-entreprene.title: Voltaire, the Entrepreneur

aneesh/summaries/walking-the-world-machi.summary: Patrick Atwater's personal essay connecting Paul Salopek's 'Out of Eden Walk' slow journalism project to the World Machines framework, with speculative extensions on pre-Axial history, numerals, domestication, and the 'cyberpaleo' approach to liveness.
aneesh/summaries/walking-the-world-machi.title: Walking the World Machines

aneesh/summaries/we-need-homes-in-the-de.summary: Sathe's foundational essay on space, place, and place-making: to build a home is to interrupt space; exploration of any unmapped domain — cognitive, professional, social — requires homebuilding first.
aneesh/summaries/we-need-homes-in-the-de.term: We Need Homes in the Delta Quadrant
aneesh/summaries/we-need-homes-in-the-de.title: We Need Homes in the Delta Quadrant

aneesh/summaries/weick-what-theory-is-no.summary: Karl Weick's 1995 ASQ response to Sutton and Staw argues that most theory in organizational studies is approximation, and that the five 'not theory' article elements (references, data, lists, diagrams, hypotheses) are better understood as stages in an ongoing theorizing process.
aneesh/summaries/weick-what-theory-is-no.term: What Theory Is Not, Theorizing Is
aneesh/summaries/weick-what-theory-is-no.title: What Theory Is Not, Theorizing Is

aneesh/summaries/what-do-platforms-reall.summary: Aneesh Sathe argues that digital platforms are the direct descendants of merchant-entrepreneurs and factory owners, resurrecting the boss function for the digital age through algorithmic management, creative risk-shifting, and rhetorical obfuscation.
aneesh/summaries/what-do-platforms-reall.title: What Do Platforms Really Do?

aneesh/summaries/why-every-biotech-resea.summary: A technical essay arguing that biotech research groups should adopt data lakehouse architecture (specifically DuckLake) to solve heterogeneous data management, reproducibility, and vendor lock-in problems.
aneesh/summaries/why-every-biotech-resea.term: Why Every Biotech Research Group Needs a Data Lakehouse
aneesh/summaries/why-every-biotech-resea.title: Why Every Biotech Research Group Needs a Data Lakehouse

aneesh/summaries/work-or-play-ludic-feed.summary: A personal essay tracing career decisions through the lens of ludic (play-like) feedback loop frequencies, arguing that sustainable work requires matching task cadence to one's dopamine rhythm.
aneesh/summaries/work-or-play-ludic-feed.term: Work or Play? Ludic Feedback Loops
aneesh/summaries/work-or-play-ludic-feed.title: Work or Play? Ludic Feedback Loops

aneesh/summaries/worldmachines-org-theor.summary: The canonical public-facing theory page of the World Machines Project — distilling the framework's definition, three-machine simultaneity, lifecycle structure, epistemological stance ('sensemaking triage', not GUT), and five foundational open questions. The reference document for all World Machine essays.
aneesh/summaries/worldmachines-org-theor.title: Theory — World Machines (Canonical)

aneesh/synthesis/Grammar and Its Deserte.summary: A cross-source synthesis: three distinct bodies of work — Sathe's epistemic shelter, Manaugh's Nakatomi space, and Sathe's architecture of resistance — all describe agents who survive and create by abandoning the designed grammar of their environment.
aneesh/synthesis/Grammar and Its Deserte.title: Grammar and Its Deserters

aneesh/synthesis/Place-Making and Resist.note_id: Place-Making and Resistance — The Constructive Side
aneesh/synthesis/Place-Making and Resist.summary: A synthesis connecting Sathe's shelter-as-epistemic-engine and architecture-of-resistance essays to argue that the thicket, the base camp, and Nakatomi space are all instances of the same constructive act: making place where the dominant system sees only undifferentiated space.
aneesh/synthesis/Place-Making and Resist.term: Place-Making and Resistance: The Constructive Side
aneesh/synthesis/Place-Making and Resist.title: Place-Making and Resistance: The Constructive Side

aneesh/synthesis/Stripping the Layers —.note_id: Stripping the Layers — From Spinoza to AI
aneesh/synthesis/Stripping the Layers —.summary: A long-arc synthesis connecting Spinoza's stripping of theological conceits, Hume's phenomenological minimalism, Baudrillard's consumer identity, and AI's automation of cognitive labor as successive stages in the same historical project of peeling fictions off reality.
aneesh/synthesis/Stripping the Layers —.term: Stripping the Layers: From Spinoza to AI
aneesh/synthesis/Stripping the Layers —.title: Stripping the Layers: From Spinoza to AI

aneesh/synthesis/The Opacity Turn — Thic.note_id: The Opacity Turn — Thicket, Nakatomi, Iltifat
aneesh/synthesis/The Opacity Turn — Thic.summary: A cross-source synthesis identifying opacity — the deliberate defeat of legibility-seeking systems — as a recurring concept across Sathe's architecture of resistance, Manaugh's Nakatomi space, and Adonis's iltifat, with implications for the 2025 AI context.
aneesh/synthesis/The Opacity Turn — Thic.term: The Opacity Turn: Thicket, Nakatomi, Iltifat
aneesh/synthesis/The Opacity Turn — Thic.title: The Opacity Turn: Thicket, Nakatomi, Iltifat

aneesh/synthesis/ai-homogenization-and-t.summary: The USC research on AI homogenizing cognition is the empirical instantiation of exactly what the counter-Enlightenment thinkers feared: the imposition of a single rational-universalist standard that erases the irreducible particularity of different cultures and minds.
aneesh/synthesis/ai-homogenization-and-t.title: AI Homogenization and the Counter-Enlightenment
